about: One guest room, as /en/camp is one camp: a third of the compound's guest-room block (src/components/home/compound.json, unit "rooms": two 40 ft containers joined side by side, 12.192 x 4.876 m, three rooms, front east onto a 1.5 m timber veranda under a slatted shade). Each room is 4.064 m along the block and 4.876 m deep. As in the 2026-10-25 footage (assets/reference/rooms, rooms-planned, room): on the front, a barred red-framed window left of a red door with a barred glass panel; a second barred window in the back wall; cream walls; red steel posts where the two containers were joined, across the middle of the room. No en-suite shows in the footage; the owner's brief (D-029) and the founder (2026-10-31, D-061) give every room its own shower and WC, so one is drawn across the front-left corner, under the front window, its sizes design intent [A]. The floor is bare plywood today; it is drawn in the studio's oak planks, and the furniture in the studio's Medium Oak. The 2D (guest-room-plan.tsx) and the 3D (scripts/site/render/guest-room.html) both read this file. Plan in metres: x to the right along the block, y toward the front (the door), the room's centre at 0,0. Furniture sizes and places are design choices, not yet sourced.

block.about: The room's share of the block, outside the steel: 12.192 / 3 long, two container widths deep. The stone plinth lifts it 0.3 m; the floor sits on the container's 0.14 m bottom rail.

room.about: Inside the linings: partitions to the neighbouring rooms left and right, the containers' long walls front and back. Ceiling height after the cove seen in the footage.

joint.about: Where the two containers were joined, the middle wall is gone; two red steel posts stand against the partitions and a beam runs overhead, as in the footage.

door.about: Red steel door with a barred glass panel in its upper half, hinged on the right, opening in against the right wall.

window.about: Red-framed, barred, opening outward: one on the front left of the door, one in the back wall over the bed.

veranda.about: Timber boards the length of the block, 1.5 m deep, a step down in front of each door, a slatted shade overhead on posts along its edge (shown dashed in the 2D, left off the 3D so the room shows). Under the window, two slatted chairs and a small round table, as on the camp's porch.

bed.about: A 160 x 200 cm double, headboard against the back wall under its window, white bedding, two pillows, a mustard throw at the foot.

bedsides.about: A bedside table each side with a linen-shade lamp.

bench.about: Luggage bench across the foot of the bed.

wardrobe.about: Two-door wardrobe on the left wall, beside the bed, between the left bedside table and the joint post.

desk.about: A small desk on the right wall, beside the bed's foot and short of the joint post, its chair facing the wall; the front window now lights the bathroom (D-061).

hooks.about: A rail of coat hooks on the right wall, clear of the door's swing.

rug.about: Woven rug under the lower two thirds of the bed.

bath.about: The en-suite (D-061): a lined stud partition across the room's front-left corner, from the left partition to just short of the door, the front window now its window (frosted lower pane, opening out, the room's only ventilation for the shower until an extract fan is chosen) [A]. A sliding door on the room side, sliding left along the partition, so no swing. Inside, along the front wall: a walk-in shower on a 900 x 900 tray with a fixed glass screen and the instant heater on the left wall, as the studio's (D-053); a floor-standing WC with its low cistern under the window's sill; a basin on a timber console with a mirror. Plan metres as the room's; the shower, WC and basin sizes are the studio's and the public bathroom's choices, not yet sourced.

electric.about: The room's wiring in the studio's pattern (D-021): its own surface unit board, a double-pole main switch and type 2 surge protection, one RCBO 30 mA type A per circuit, cables in conduit in the linings. The supply is a cable from the farm's site board (the power guide); its size is the electrician's, to the run's length. Points in plan metres (x, y as the plan, z above the floor) at their centre, facing out of their wall; size in mm (w, h, d). design_A: lights and the fan from their watts at 230 V; sockets and the AC provision at the studio's design loads (C2 and C7). rwf: the studio BOM's placeholder unit prices (AS-21), not quotes. The en-suite (D-061) adds the studio's 5.5 kW instant shower heater on its own B25 circuit in 6 mm² (C4), with a double-pole isolator outside the bathroom, so the main switch rises to 63 A as the studio's (D-053) [A]; the bathroom light is IP44, on the lights circuit.

circuits.serves: Sockets: the bed, the desk and the cleaning socket

points.description: Unit board, 12 modules, on the right wall by the bed
Ceiling light, by the door and the desk
Two-gang switch by the door, past its swing: L1 and L2
Switch for the bathroom light, outside its door
Wall fan 300 mm, high on the left wall over the bed
Socket + USB-C beside the left bedside table, for its lamp and a phone
Socket + USB-C beside the right bedside table, for its lamp and a phone
Double socket over the desk, for its lamp and a laptop
Double socket on the left wall by the bathroom: cleaning, a kettle
AC provision: isolator high on the back wall, for a split unit later
Shower heater double-pole isolator, outside the bathroom
Instant shower heater 5.5 kW, IPX4, on the shower's left wall
Smoke alarm, 10-year battery, on the ceiling by the door
